answer.Text: The characteristic polynomial is merely a mathematical device to collect the eigenvalues into one object, Michael. Although it is thus extraordinarily useful, it can also obscure what is going on. Both geometrically and algebraically, we are selecting a new basis for a vector space and studying the process from that new point of view. This decomposes the process into a linear combination of one-dimensional processes. The root of each is just a multiplier: that leads to the statement I made. Moreover, these roots usually are found by methods that *avoid* solving the characteristic polynomial!
